title: MCP server overview
claims: MCP distinguishes user-controlled prompts, application-controlled resources and model-controlled tools.
notes: Use the control distinction when mapping adapters.

title: The 2026-07-28 MCP specification
claims: The revision removes protocol-level Streamable HTTP sessions and uses explicit server-minted handles for cross-call state.
List/read responses gain ttlMs and cacheScope; authorization guidance adds issuer validation.
notes: Version-aware source; implementation was not tested.

title: MCP key changes
claims: Streamable HTTP request headers and deterministic tool listing are documented.
OpenTelemetry trace context propagation conventions are documented for MCP metadata.
notes: Draft changelog; pin exact protocol revision in an implementation.

title: MCP Tasks extension overview
claims: tasks/cancel expresses cooperative cancellation intent.
The Tasks extension currently augments tools/call and supports task status notifications.
notes: Do not equate task cancellation with OS process teardown.

tool: ACP v2 is available in Draft
title: ACP v2 is available in Draft
claims: ACP v2 is draft and should be version-negotiated alongside v1.
v2 describes session updates outside prompt turns, stable-ID patch semantics, structured file changes and flexible permission requests.
notes: ACP means Agent Client Protocol in this document.

title: ACP TCK
claims: The TCK checks that agents do not call client methods whose capabilities were not advertised.
It covers version negotiation, session cancellation, permission flow, stdio JSON-RPC and resume/replay behavior.
notes: Test-suite documentation, not a local test result.

title: A2A v1.0.1 specification
claims: A2A uses Agent Cards, stateful Tasks, Messages and Artifacts with polling, streaming and optional push updates.
Clients must validate declared capability support and send a compatible major.minor protocol version.
notes: Version-specific primary specification.

title: A2A agent discovery
claims: A2A documentation recommends out-of-band dynamic credentials rather than static secrets in Agent Cards.
notes: Discovery metadata is not an authorization grant.

title: E2B security
claims: E2B documents a Firecracker microVM with dedicated kernel per sandbox.
Sandbox state can persist across pause/resume and sandboxes are destroyed on timeout or shutdown.
notes: Provider claim; no penetration or lifecycle test performed.

title: Daytona Sandboxes
claims: Daytona documents hypervisor-isolated virtual machines with lifecycle and persistence.
The toolbox can expose code/process/filesystem/Git/PTY/computer-use/LSP/log capabilities.
notes: Provider claim; exact selected capabilities must be recorded per run.

title: Modal Sandboxes
claims: Modal documents lifecycle events and explicit termination for Sandboxes.
It exposes gVisor and VM runtime choices.
notes: Runtime choice is not a complete network or secret policy.

title: Browser Use Browser Harness
claims: Browser Use documents control of the user's Chrome profile including tabs, cookies and logins.
It distinguishes local real-browser and cloud-browser operation.
notes: Treat authenticated browser control as high-impact authority.

title: OpenTelemetry general semantic conventions
claims: OpenTelemetry publishes semantic conventions for spans, metrics, logs and events.
notes: Conventions alone do not guarantee audit completeness or redaction.

title: Langfuse masking
claims: Langfuse supports masking trace/observation input, output and metadata before data leaves an application.
mask_otel_spans operates at export stage for OpenTelemetry spans.
notes: Export masking does not replace application-side secret minimization.

title: Arize Phoenix
claims: Phoenix is an open-source observability/evaluation tool using OpenTelemetry and OpenInference.
notes: No collector or evaluation workflow was run.

title: ATIF specification
claims: ATIF is a JSON format for complete autonomous-agent interaction histories.
It supports run-scoped trajectories and subagent/continuation relationships.
notes: Trajectory exports require independent access control/redaction.

title: SWE-bench FAQ
claims: SWE-bench evaluates patches by preparing Docker environments, applying patches and running tests.
It lists full, Lite, Verified, Multimodal and Multilingual datasets.
notes: Benchmark result is not a general reliability claim.

title: Terminal-Bench 4.0
claims: Terminal-Bench 4.0 is the current documented run version and uses Harbor.
Major versions require rerun when agent-environment/task/resource changes occur; 4.0 removes saturated tasks and recalibrates resources.
notes: Do not call Terminal-Bench 2.0 latest.

title: Terminal-Bench releases
claims: The official v4.0.0 release documents the dataset invocation terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0.
notes: No benchmark command was executed.

title: MCP authorization 2026-07-28
claims: HTTP authorization defines issuer-bound discovery/response validation and resource targeting; stdio uses a separate credential model.
notes: Selected primary source inspected; runtime, conformance and product quality remain unqualified.

title: Supporting protocol revision 2026-07-28
claims: Documented 2026 authorization requirements need explicit SDK opt-ins; wire negotiation alone is not proof.
notes: Selected primary source inspected; runtime, conformance and product quality remain unqualified.

title: Agent Skills specification
claims: Directory and SKILL.md metadata constraints define a portable instruction package, not a permission grant.
notes: Selected primary source inspected; runtime, conformance and product quality remain unqualified.

title: AGENTS.md project guidance
claims: Repository instructions provide project context; host enforcement and discovery still depend on the consumer.
notes: Selected primary source inspected; runtime, conformance and product quality remain unqualified.
